findings.title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource then shares the same stale timestamp. The fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: datetime in task kwargs breaks JSON serialization and the cycle check
findings.body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict`, so the payload contains a raw `datetime` in `queued`. Celery's JSON serializer either rejects it or turns it into a string. If it becomes a string, the frozen dataclass still accepts it at the worker, so the type is silently wrong. If serialization fails, the outbound task is never enqueued. The datetime should be converted to an ISO string or timestamp before enqueuing and parsed back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to integrations that don't accept it
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. Concrete implementations (Jira, VSTS, GitHub, etc.) were not updated in this PR. Any implementation whose signature lacks `**kwargs` will raise TypeError, breaking outbound assignee sync for that provider.

findings.title: Abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature changed but never used
findings.body: `assignment_source` was added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature, but no caller passes it. Status-sync cycles are therefore not addressed, and the signature now disagrees with the subclasses.
